q: Can I use my coal's lab carbon content instead of a default factor?
title: Coal carbon content from lab tests
short: Yes, and it is often more accurate. If a lab gives the carbon percentage on an as-received basis, CO2 equals carbon mass times 44/12, with full oxidation as the IPCC 2006 default assumes. Use the same basis as the weight you burned, and test each lot or a fixed schedule.
audience: Boiler, kiln and captive power operators burning coal

p: CO2 (t) = coal burned (t, as received) x carbon fraction (as received) x 44/12.

ul: Air-dried or dry-basis results must be converted to as-received using total moisture.
Sample to a written method, so results represent the lot.
Keep lab certificates with the invoices.

p: For small users, the IPCC default by coal type or a GCV-based estimate is accepted. State which you used.
